models.model_label: OLS time-trend regression for propensity to avoid quarterly losses
models.sample_description: One annual standardized-difference statistic per calendar year, 1985–2002 (18 regression observations), for the avoid quarterly losses threshold. The yearly statistics are calculated from the main firm-quarter data, using the bin immediately left of zero and a common standardized sample size of 1,000. The underlying main-analysis firm-quarter sample totals 111,485 observations over 1985–2002; those firm-quarter counts are not the N for this time-trend regression.
models.method_reported: OLS regression of standardized differences on year
models.method_details: The dependent variable is the yearly Burgstahler–Dichev standardized difference for the specified threshold; the slope on calendar year assesses temporal change in propensity.

dependent_variable.name: Standardized difference: avoid quarterly losses
dependent_variable.definition: Burgstahler–Dichev standardized difference for the avoid-loss threshold (quarterly earnings level deflated by beginning-of-quarter-t stock price) in year y, evaluated in the earnings bin just left of zero. It is the actual observation count minus the expected count, divided by the estimated standard deviation of that difference; the expected count is the average of the two adjacent bins. The authors compute the threshold-year statistic using a standardized N of 1,000 based on the actual bin proportion. Bins have width .0025. A negative value indicates threshold achievement; |statistic| ≥ 2.33 is the stated one-tailed threshold criterion.
dependent_variable.formula: SDiff_avoid-loss,y = (Observed_left_bin_y − Expected_left_bin_y) / EstimatedSD(Observed − Expected); Expected_left_bin_y = mean(counts in adjacent bins); counts rescaled to N=1,000.

review_notes: Source-first scope: select the threshold-propensity family for the paper’s principal RQ1. The authors say the primary analysis uses the Burgstahler–Dichev threshold statistic and that OLS regressions of its annual standardized differences on year assess temporal change. Retain one regression for each of the three parallel threshold outcomes (Figure 1).

Exclude the repeated annual CAR regressions in Table 1 as the downstream valuation rationale (RQ2) for the propensity shift, despite the title and their prominent results table. Exclude RQ3/RQ4 forecast accuracy and precision analyses as further explanations; exclude the five sensitivity checks. These are separate downstream questions, not additional baselines for the selected propensity hierarchy.
descriptive_reason: Targeted review of the selected baseline methods and Figure 1 pages 6–8 found no means, standard deviations, percentiles, or other exact summary-statistic rows for Year or the annual standardized-difference dependent series. Figure 1 plots the yearly series and labels each trend slope/adjusted R-square, but it does not provide exact yearly values or data-value descriptive summaries.
results_review_notes: Only the three frozen Figure 1 trend models are included. The yearly point values in Figure 1 were not approximated from the plotted lines.

calculation_provenance.policy: strict; no guessed degrees of freedom or normal approximations
